comparison: Perfect alignment on computational modeling of supercomplex organization (C60-C65). Both evaluations find the modeling analysis and inference about coexisting variants well-supported, with no concerns raised about methodology or interpretation.

Perfect alignment on spatial overlap analysis and interdigitation patterns (C66-C72). Both evaluations support the quantitative measurements and visualization of PSII-PSI organization across stacked membranes.

Strong agreement on the distinction between intact and ruptured chloroplasts (C73-C74, C91-C93). Both note the non-crystalline organization in intact samples versus lattices in ruptured samples. OpenEval notes mechanistic interpretation is somewhat speculative; peer reviewers accept this as supporting evidence for native state.

Strong agreement on main conclusions about two-domain model and absence of grana margin (C6, C8-C10, C89). Peer reviewers explicitly praise this as 'strong evidence challenging long-standing assumptions.' OpenEval notes domain boundary fluidity inference (C90) is reasonable but not directly tested.

Both evaluations rate the condensation model as UNCERTAIN/speculative (C97-C104, overlapping on C98, C100-C104). OpenEval notes lack of direct experimental validation; peer reviewers did not explicitly comment but authors acknowledge inability to directly track movements.

Agreement on technical limitations (C106-C109). Both evaluations support the transparent discussion of extraction artifacts, preferential orientation, and sampling bias. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledged these limitations while rating reliability as 'high.'

Agreement on uniform PSII distribution findings (C59, C87-C88). Peer reviewers explicitly noted 'PSII did not form a semi-crystalline array and was distributed uniformly.' Both evaluations support this as part of evidence for the two-domain model.

Agreement on comparative analysis with C. reinhardtii and A. thaliana (C56-C58). Peer reviewers noted the study demonstrates 'molecular organization in spinach thylakoids closely mirrors' earlier Chlamydomonas research. Both evaluations support the quantitative comparisons.

Partial overlap on AI-assisted particle detection methodology (C53-C55 in OpenEval R3, C5 in peer R1). Both evaluations praise the computational approach. Peer reviewers explicitly noted 'advanced AI-based image analysis' and 'successfully quantifies' findings.

Both address AI-assisted computational methodology (C5). OpenEval R13 focuses on methodological description and validation; peer R1 explicitly praises the AI-driven tools with no concerns about methodology or quantification.

Partial overlap on grana ultrastructural features (C23-C30). OpenEval R1 covers broad cryo-ET methodology and architectural observations; peer R7 specifically notes 'detailed ultrastructural features of grana membranes' with no concerns about validity.

Partial overlap on grana architecture and helical staircase model (C31-C36, C76-C77). OpenEval R1 presents quantitative morphometric data; peer R8 implicitly accepts architectural observations as part of overall structural characterization.

Partial overlap on high-resolution structural measurements (C37-C40, C82). OpenEval R1 emphasizes quantitative data with error estimates; peer R6 praises 'single-molecule precision' and high-resolution data quality.

Partial overlap on photosynthetic complex spatial segregation (C43-C46). OpenEval R2 covers membranogram visualizations showing segregation; peer R9 implicitly supports identification of cytb6f in appressed membranes as consistent with two-domain model.

Partial overlap on absence of grana margin heterogeneity (C50, C86). OpenEval R2 notes this contradicts some biochemical studies but is directly visualized; peer R4 implicitly supports as part of two-domain model acceptance.

Minimal overlap on spatial segregation findings (C51, C84). Both evaluations support the pronounced lateral segregation of PSII and PSI. Peer reviewers explicitly noted this as part of evidence for absence of specialized grana margin zone.

Minimal overlap on uniform PSII distribution (C7). OpenEval R7 includes this as part of main conclusions synthesis; peer R3 explicitly supports uniform distribution finding as evidence for two-domain model.

Minimal overlap on mechanistic interpretation (C95-C96). OpenEval R6 notes inference about free mixing is reasonable but indirect; peer R13 treats condensation model as speculative hypothesis requiring further testing.
OpenEval R10 addresses plant growth conditions (C115-C117) as standard methodological details. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.
OpenEval R11 addresses established background knowledge and literature context (C1, C4, C11-C18, C113-C114). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.

OpenEval R12 addresses citations to authors' previous work (C2-C3, C19-C20) providing context for extending methods to vascular plants. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific citation claims.
